newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cochlear encouraged by 1st half sales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cochlear encouraged by 1st half sales.

text.p: Cochlear Ltd has experienced strong demand for its new bionic ear model and was encouraged by its first half results despite a fall in earnings, the company's managing director, Catherine Livingstone said.

"In terms of the impact on sales, it was the first six months that had no contribution from (Spectra 22) upgrades. We have achieved the growth in sales that we were aiming for without the Spectra upgrades, which we are very pleased about," Livingstone told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Cohlear earlier said its net profit for the six months to December 31 fell 11.8 percent to A$4.52 million.
Livingstone said the company maintained its forecast of flat net earnings for the year to June 30, 1997.
"Our expectations are that (year net) earnings will be in the range of A$10.5 million to A$10.9 million," Livingstone said.
Cochlear reported full year net earnings of A$10.86 million for the 1995/96 financial year.

Cochlear's chief financial officer, Neville Mitchell said the fall in first half earnings was mostly due to the strength of the Australian dollar which he said effectively reduced the company's first half net earnings by about A$1 million.

Mitchell said the Australian government's reduction of the research and development tax concession last year had reduced its net earnings by about A$500,000 in the first half and was expected to have the same effect in the second half.

"All research and development (R&D) projects were reviewed in light of the tax concession reduction. This review resulted in R&D being held constant at the previous years expenditure level," the company said.
Cochlear said its manufacturing yields were improved and selling and said other operating costs were controlled at levels comparable with last year.
Cochlear paid a fully franked dividend of five cents a share and the company said it expected its full year dividend to be maintained at 7.5 cents.
At 2.10 p.m (0310 GMT), Cohlear shares were steady at A$3.75.
